conclusions: T6 manner: force level is controllable (mean hold monotone in closure stop over R1-R4), speed is realised ~1:1, task success 100% and contact-clean 88% on every cfg; but the strict window criterion (whole hold window inside an 8 N band) is met for only 59/240 requests because the thin-wall pinch lets the mug shift in hand.
Library on a new task: first-pass 14 (rule) -> 53 of 59 satisfiable; learning curve 0.57 -> 0.98 within ~100 requests; pass-within-budget 58.5/59 at lower cost than rule and oracle-order baselines.
Cross-task transfer: preloaded T0/T1/T7 rows alone (no write-back) give first-pass 37 vs rule 14; with online write-back preload adds nothing over an empty library (53.1 vs 53.2).

Repair v2 (response-based, pre-registered): large dev gain (below-band repair 42 -> 354 of 363) but FAILS on held-out T6 (pass 49.8 vs 58.5, false stops 9-34) because averaged min/max intervals mispredict a high-variance object. Not adopted as is.
